question: Can a recurrent nonlinear interaction learn useful value from causal groupwise fast/slow Kalman innovation states even though the same 39-state representation lost as an additive ridge feature?

feature_definition.raw_input: retain all 112 channels unchanged; append the existing event features and 39 new states
feature_definition.warmup_normalization: per-sequence input-channel mean and unbiased sample standard deviation over rows 0..98; scale floor 1e-6
feature_definition.filter: independent diagonal random-walk Kalman state per input channel; Q=0.001, R=1, initial level=0 and covariance=1
feature_definition.innovation: pre-update standardized residual using predicted covariance plus R; clip to [-8,8]
feature_definition.group_energy: mean squared clipped innovation per semantic group, rounded through float32 RMS exactly as the frozen reference
feature_definition.states: per group append log1p(fast EMA span=20), log1p(slow EMA span=200), and log(fast+1e-8)-log(slow+1e-8); initialize both EMAs from the first post-warmup energy; zeros on rows 0..98
feature_definition.causality: current and past input rows only; no labels, masks, sequence IDs, or future rows; all state resets per sequence

comparison.control: same model width and initialization, but all 39 added states are zeroed
comparison.treatment: same model width and initialization, with all 39 causal group states active
comparison.fit_membership: 32 source-qualified components, complete in both train and valid sources; selected deterministically from fold0 fit components using seed 20261018
comparison.evaluation_membership: all 468 evaluation groups from fold0; held out from both fits
comparison.paired: identical parent checkpoint, split, fit components, sequence order, optimizer, schedule, loss, precision, model width, and update budget; only the feature control differs

model.initializer_extension: append 39 zero-initialized input columns; inherit raw/event normalization and keep added-column mean=0 and scale=1
model.training: 1 epoch, batch=8, chunk=2000, 32 complete components, fixed epoch-0 checkpoint
model.optimizer: AdamW, lr=3e-5, weight decay=0, clip norm=1.0

metric.primary: official weighted Pearson score with fixed prediction/scored mask, clipping +/-2, and original clipped-label magnitude weights
metric.exposure: F0 has been repeatedly inspected and adaptively reused; this is exposed development evidence, not clean validation or public-transfer evidence

interpretation.useful_positive: a practical active-minus-zero gain on the paired F0 groups supports a larger B300 teacher/student interaction study; it does not establish a clean-fold or public gain
interpretation.weak_or_negative: defer this one seed, one exposed panel, and feature-scale treatment; preserve the retained-raw Kalman teacher/student direction in PR #17
interpretation.uncertainty: one fitting seed and one repeatedly exposed evaluation fold; component resampling is conditional on these fixed fit checkpoints and does not cover fit-seed, fold, or public-transfer uncertainty
interpretation.no_kill_rule: an interval crossing zero does not alone close this mechanism; the screen informs whether to allocate the predeclared 30-paired-cell B300 confirmation
